scope: Runner RPC recovery after upstream Hub disconnect, stale acknowledgement isolation, and authoritative project ownership for Hub RPC registrations and responses.
status: Approved after actual Claude Opus 5.5 closure of the final source delta; no unresolved blocking findings in the reviewed scope.

designDecisions.proposal: Close the downstream Engine.IO transport on upstream disconnect to trigger native CLI reconnect.
designDecisions.disposition: Rejected after source inspection: native ApiSessionClient closes its terminal subprocesses on disconnect, so normal short-lived capability rotation would introduce repeated terminal termination.

designDecisions.proposal: Replay the current, bounded set of declarative RPC method registrations.
designDecisions.disposition: Accepted: only normalized method names are retained, with bounded count and UTF-8 size; unregister updates the current set immediately; replay precedes the existing pending live-event queue. No invocation or acknowledgement replay cache is introduced.

designDecisions.proposal: Trust a registration prefix matching the downstream handshake.
designDecisions.disposition: Rejected as an authority boundary: handshake identifiers are untrusted. The Hub independently checks the authenticated namespace against the current stored target and current capability.

findings.cause: Upstream reconnect removed the Hub registry entries while the still-connected native CLI had no reason to register its methods again.
findings.resolution: Per downstream connection retain only its current normalized method names; replay before pending events on upstream connect. Limits: 256 methods, 64 KiB total, 512 UTF-8 bytes per method and 128 per scope identifier. Reject invalid/new overflow entries without evicting existing registrations or forcing downstream disconnect.

findings.cause: A delayed acknowledgement to an old Hub request could be sent by the reused upstream client object into a newer Hub connection with a reused acknowledgement ID.
findings.resolution: Forwarded acknowledgement callbacks are bound to the upstream connection generation and drop after disconnect, replacement or proxy closure.

findings.cause: Global method registration accepted claimed target identifiers without verifying ownership in the authenticated namespace.
findings.resolution: Registration requires declared scope consistency plus a fresh server-side session/machine lookup in the authenticated namespace and current live authorization; untrusted handshake fields cannot supply authority.

findings.cause: An identical textual ID for a session and a machine could collide in a global method key.
findings.resolution: Registry keys and gateway lookup distinguish session and machine kinds while retaining the existing wire method string.

findings.cause: A previously valid target could be deleted, moved, revoked or re-registered while an RPC was pending.
findings.resolution: Registry entries retain a fresh authority validator; lookup before dispatch is fail-closed. After acknowledgement the gateway requires the exact same still-authorized registration entry. Old unregister/disconnect cannot remove a replacement registration.

findings.cause: Machine IDs may contain colons. A runner authorized for target a could register a method whose concatenation matched the method for a distinct target a:b if lookup used only kind and method.
findings.resolution: Registry keys are structural tuples of kind, exact target ID and method. Stored authority includes the exact ID; the gateway passes the original target ID both before dispatch and after acknowledgement. A real cross-namespace colon-ID regression verifies that the foreign target receives no dispatch.

findings.cause: Replacing an entry for an identical declarative registration could unnecessarily invalidate a legitimate pending response.
findings.resolution: An identical same-socket registration preserves the entry. Explicit unregister followed by register creates a new entry and invalidates the old pending acknowledgement.

findings.cause: Treating an invalidated reply as a target missing before dispatch could hide that an operation had already executed, including rewind actions.
findings.resolution: RpcResponseInvalidatedError distinguishes a sent request whose authority or entry changed before acknowledgement from RpcTargetMissingError. Its message states that the action may have completed; existing generic uncertain-outcome handling remains active.

limits: This is an internal source/design review with actual model identity recorded, not an external security certification.

Existing bounded pending live-event behavior is retained. Overflow, genuine authorization loss or process shutdown can still disconnect a client; uninterrupted terminal restoration across a real Hub restart is not claimed.
The fix deliberately avoids introducing periodic downstream disconnection during normal capability renewal. It does not redesign the Hub terminal registry or native agent process lifecycle.
Supported current native session and machine clients declare their scope. Undeclared, forged, cross-namespace or otherwise invalid RPC registrations are rejected.
Within one authenticated project namespace, authorized runners remain trusted to serve that project. The web/API caller must independently pass its existing project/namespace access checks.

No provider-account login, paid inference, publication, deployed-version verification or anonymous-access result is claimed by this source review. The coordinator performs final integration/deployment/publication verification.
Earlier public-launch review records and their historical source/test hashes remain unchanged.
A temporary store/authority-check failure fails closed and may remove a registration until the next valid CLI registration or upstream replay. No availability fallback bypasses ownership checks.
Post-dispatch invalidation does not undo an operation that may already have run. Its distinct error preserves uncertain-outcome handling; no automatic replay of that action is introduced.

closureNotes.disposition: The narrow closure excerpt omitted the registration wiring; this was a supplied-context limitation, not a new finding. The coordinator independently checked the final source: registerRpcHandlers in hub/src/socket/handlers/cli/index.ts compares the current socket namespace, invokes the live isAuthorized check when present, and resolves sessions with fresh:true or performs a fresh machine lookup. The complete wiring had already been supplied in the preceding full adversarial source review.

RPC scope identifiers must be nonempty, at most 128 UTF-8 bytes, and contain no colon, whitespace or control characters. Supported native IDs conform; custom machine IDs accepted by the broader creation schema may be unable to register RPC methods. This fail-closed boundary is explicit and the colon-target alias regression prevents routing them to another target.
